searchText: do I understand correctly that with eip-4488, we stop pricing 0-bytes differently and just price all bytes the same? This is how the reference Geth implementation does now: https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/compare/master...quilt:calldata-eip?expand=1#diff-8c398ef0a79f97ba6d497a99247a815b3a51918de9e16954215b6073f907c92eR128-R133 Yep, from the EIP ``` Reduce the gas cost of transaction calldata to NEW_CALLDATA_GAS_COST per byte, regardless of whether the byte is zero or nonzero. ``` 65/67 of those blocks > 1MB of calldata happened between Jan 12 and Jan 13th 2020. Weird. <dannyryan> they they were almost certainly a part of the starkware experiment https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/eip-2028-transaction-data-gas-cost-reduction/3280/35?u=djrtwo <dannyryan> “big red dot" <dannyryan> > On January 12 2020 (after Istanbul and Muir Glacier), we repeated the experiment. Thus, StarkWare is also responsible for the new Big Red Dot. awesome, thanks for the background Juat checking here, for EIP 4444, what happens to tx data after one year has passed? Is there like an option to keep it for archiving purposes or it's gone forever (at least for the local copy)? Nodes can choose to keep it longer And if a client wants to get that history, they could use a light client protocol to do that the idea was to make it unavailable over devp2p or at least over `eth` devp2p subprotocol Anyone know what the deal is with Kovan today? No new blocks on etherscan in an hour, we are ahead of what they report but peering is super spotty (most nodes only have 2-3 peers). I'm not sure where Kovan is discussed these days so asking here, if someone can point me to the proper place thanks! I _think_ XDAI has taken over OE maintenance, but it's a bit unclear. I'd assume this includes Kovan. Their discord has an #openethereum channel. I can't send an invite. Anyone in <@&595684226221735986> can? Thanks Tim I am in that Discord, I'll ask over there. Hmm doesnt look like I have "send" access in the kovan channel over there though.

excerpts.author: lukaszrozmej
excerpts.content:
do I understand correctly that with eip-4488, we stop pricing 0-bytes differently and just price all bytes the same?

This is how the reference Geth implementation does now: https://github.com/ethereum/go-ethereum/compare/master...quilt:calldata-eip?expand=1#diff-8c398ef0a79f97ba6d497a99247a815b3a51918de9e16954215b6073f907c92eR128-R133

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content:
Yep, from the EIP
```
Reduce the gas cost of transaction calldata to NEW_CALLDATA_GAS_COST per byte, regardless of whether the byte is zero or nonzero.
```
